# Website and API deployment

`alchemy.run.ts` declares the Cloudflare API and Website for one stage. The
API is declared first; the Website receives the API's address and private
binding. Deploy them together so each stage's pair matches.

| Stage | Doppler config | Website | API |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prod` | `taxkit/prd` | `https://taxkit.dev` (`www` redirects) | `https://api.taxkit.dev` |
| `pr-<number>` | `taxkit/stg_preview` | the stage's `workers.dev` address | the stage's `workers.dev` address |
| `dev_native_apps` | none (local) | printed by `bun run dev` | printed by `bun run dev` |

Deploying needs the maintainer's explicit request. The commands run locally
from a clean checkout of the commit being deployed.

## Credentials

Native Alchemy reads the stage's Doppler config, then an ignored `.env`, and
never the shell environment. The Doppler config holds that stage's Cloudflare
account ID and API token. Alchemy authenticates to Doppler with `DOPPLER_TOKEN`
or an Alchemy profile login; locally, pass the repository's existing Doppler
login for the one command without printing it:

```sh
DOPPLER_TOKEN="$(doppler configure get token --plain)" bun run production:plan
```

Do not copy Cloudflare values into the shell, a committed file or GitHub.

## Preview

```sh
bun run pr:plan pr-<number>
bun run pr:deploy pr-<number>
bun run pr:destroy pr-<number>
```

`pr:deploy` builds the repository first. Preview uses its own API, never the
Production API. Destroy the stage when its pull request closes.

## Production

```sh
bun run production:plan
bun run production:deploy
bun run production:drift
```

Review the plan. Production adopts and retains the `taxkit.dev` zone and DNS
settings; a plan that would create, replace or delete the zone, or delete either
Worker, must stop. `production:drift` compares the deployed resources with
state.

## Check the deployment

1. Note both Worker version IDs from the deploy output.
2. Load the Website, a docs page and its `.md` page; calculate with and without
   JavaScript.
3. Check `https://www.taxkit.dev/<path>?<query>` returns a 301 to the same path
   and query on `taxkit.dev`.
4. Check API CORS from a browser page on another origin: public GETs and the
   calculation POST are allowed without credentials.
5. Repeat an eligible public GET with the same headers. The second response
   should show `CF-Cache-Status: HIT` and an `Age`. Calculation results,
   errors and `Set-Cookie` replies stay private and uncached.

## Rollback

Check out the previous working commit and run the same deploy command for the
stage. Cloudflare caches are version-scoped, so the redeployed versions start
with empty caches. Activation of the two Workers is not atomic; a short overlap
of old and new versions is possible.

## Known limits

- The native Alchemy redirect provider treats a failed read of the zone's
  shared redirect ruleset as an empty ruleset. A later successful write then
  holds only TaxKit's `www` rule and can remove redirect rules owned elsewhere
  in the zone. The `taxkit.dev` zone holds only TaxKit's own rule; check the
  zone's redirect rules before adding another owner. The Worker upload happens
  before the redirect rule is written.
- Seven-day Cloudflare freshness lets Cloudflare reuse a response; it does not
  guarantee that the cache keeps it.

the Website memo includes the shared packages), so a content-only change

platform records can include caller URLs. Application diagnostics use fixed

change proof. Cross-process creation races remain a limitation of the provider
API; duplicate ownership fails on a subsequent complete inventory. The app stack still collects off
and has no PostHog project reference or management credentials in its bindings.
Browser sender choice, capture wiring, stored-event readback and any real
operation remain separately tracked T008 work. Metrics remain deferred.

## Disposable local apps

`alchemy.apps.local.run.ts` uses the same `declareNativeAppsStack` resource
graph with `Alchemy.localState()`. Its native context check rejects operations
other than development, remote provider mode and stages outside
`dev_native_apps` / `dev_native_apps_proof` before declaring either resource.
The root `dev` command supplies an empty owned env file and an isolated
`ALCHEMY_HOME`; it does not construct the cloud stack or Doppler secrets.
Native resources own the addresses, bindings and local Worker/Vite lifetimes.
The [Website README](../../apps/web/README.md) owns contributor setup and the
saved real-CLI development test. Local state is disposable development evidence,
not cloud provider or deployment proof.

## Calculator platform records

The API app export owns `ApiWorkerObservability`. The native apps graph uses it
for the API and declares the Website's separate disabled settings. Global
collection, invocation logs, stored logs and traces are all explicitly disabled,
with zero sampling. Omitting these properties would select Alchemy's default
invocation logs, which can contain caller URLs outside the app's fixed reporter.

Native mock plans and saved real local CLI state must both contain those settings.
Removing the API graph settings fails the saved local-state check. This proves
the declared local policy, not a Cloudflare upload or exported data. The
standalone Website's `wrangler.jsonc` carries matching disabled settings. The
existing docs app keeps its own policy. T009 still owes safe exported tracing;
disabling collection does not complete that requirement.


## Native calculation limiter configuration

`NativeAppsHostMode` defaults to `edge`. The graph binds that mode to both native
apps as `CALCULATOR_HOST_MODE`. The API app's native admission Layer registers
one 60/60 RateLimit binding and captures required checked
`CALCULATOR_RATE_NAMESPACE` through Alchemy's own Config/runtime bridge.
The native cloud secret composition supplies non-secret namespace `10078` for
Production and `10078` followed by the checked PR number for each Preview.
These values take precedence over the selected Doppler config; shell app values
remain disabled. Different Preview stages and Production have separate counters.
Development retains its selected configuration. Before cloud apply,
independently read every available Worker binding and refuse a foreign namespace
collision. The dated deployment receipt owns that account observation; the
declaration alone cannot reserve a provider namespace.

The guarded disposable root supplies `local-emulator` and isolated local
namespace `10075`. It cannot select a cloud stage or provider mode. API and
Website additionally require an HTTP loopback API origin before using their one
shared local allowance. Native graph tests keep create/no-change/update checks
and forbid provider writes. Their saved state uses Alchemy's own packed
Config representation, including the captured namespace, rather than omitting
new native settings from the no-change fixture.

The deployment runbook preserves old `DocsWebsite` operations as stopped
history and separately owns native preparation. Cooper's current active plan
authorises qualified Preview and Production deployment from this Mac. Each
operation still needs its exact candidate, namespace readback, receipt and
recovery. Local limiter tests cannot establish real edge or cloud state.


## Native older-client conversation host

The API app's native composition registers `TaxKitMcpSessions`. The SDK adds its
Durable Object export and binding to the actual API resource. The Website does
not export this class. Graph tests check this distinction in their memory-only
create/no-change/update cases; no namespace ID or provider setting is invented.
The app owns one fixed-name host per stage, with bounded in-memory conversations
and native alarm expiry. Only alarm bookkeeping uses storage. The
[API owner](../../apps/api/README.md#native-remote-calculator-tools-candidate)
explains limits, private original-key forwarding, separate instance pools and
the documented modern five-second cancellation limit.

The local native source builder compiles the actual API declaration using
memory state to obtain the SDK-generated class export inventory. Every provider,
credential and network operation refuses. It runs no provider plan/apply or
saved-state operation. The local emulator binds this generated class to isolated
fixture namespaces. The cloud API/Website operation remains DEV-81 work,
including exact class migration/binding readback and rollback; current local
proof does not approve or establish that operation.


## Production-only domain candidate

The native `prod` graph declares an adopted retained `taxkit.dev` zone and
retained DNS settings matching the independent 7 October readback. It declares
`taxkit.dev` for the Website, a native `www.taxkit.dev` redirect, and
`api.taxkit.dev` for the API. Domain zone IDs come from the declared zone's
Output. Self origins still use `Worker.URL`; peer origins still use resource
Outputs and checked application Config. Local and `pr-N` graphs omit domain
properties and both Production resources; they do not request domain removal.

The [dated provider readback](../../docs/documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/2026-10-07-domain-provider-readback.json)
records existing state, not desired availability. DNSSEC, registrar lock,
automatic renewal, TLS settings, SOA and unrelated records are not changed by
this declaration. The focused native graph uses memory state, mocked reads and
refused writes. The installed Alchemy beta.80 redirect provider originally treated every failed
shared-rule read as an empty ruleset. Actual mocked-provider calls reproduced
that behaviour. The receiving source and compiled provider are now patched to
accept only native `RulesetNotFound` as absence: a 403 refuses rule replacement,
a specific missing-rule reply permits creation, and existing unrelated rules
survive. The three regular provider tests and six source/compiled probes pass.
The provider uploads its Worker script before reading shared redirect rules;
this correction does not roll that earlier upload back after a read failure.

The version-three plan projection in `tools/docs-deployment` admits the native
API/Website resources, checked bindings and summary. Its Production variant
also admits the retained settings and adopted zone; zone creation, replacement,
delete, unknown rows and Production resources in Preview refuse. It requires
the exact configured account and Production zone. The existing projection
command now checks a clean candidate and unchanged tracked source bytes,
calculates configuration/input/lockfile/patch hashes, and writes a separate
native source identity. Optional supplied hashes must agree. The manifest
covers the named source paths; generated/dependency bytes, environment and
provider state remain outside it. Installed beta.80 version and caller-supplied
plan shape do not prove installed patch equality or the plan's origin.
Historical version-one/two receipts keep their original bytes and resource
identities, and historical writer commands/workflows still refuse. Native
bootstrap/provider receipts, live no-apply plans and full secret custody/readback
remain T007/DEV-81 work. No actual adoption, attachment, certificate, apply or
public runtime is established here. The deployment tool README and runbook own
source coverage, required command inputs and partial local-write recovery.
and SDK contracts, public accepted documentation and the five existing runbook
procedures. This versioned private package follows the
[Changeset rules](../../docs/standards/versioning.md); package-facing changes
include their own Changeset outside the public tax/SDK release group.

The [deployment runbook](../../docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md) and

plans, authority, retained projects, recovery and readback. Tests use controlled
transports and synthetic capture tokens; they perform no provider operation.
Local and ordinary Preview collection must stay off. Production or a controlled
Preview requires checked settings and separately qualified app composition.

fixed publication address `https://taxkit.dev`. Nothing in the API depends on
the Website, so unpatched Alchemy plans the graph without a binding cycle.

Both Workers declare version-scoped native caching, and the Website's build memo
includes the shared packages so content changes rebuild it. Platform invocation
logs, stored logs and traces are disabled on both because platform records can
include caller URLs.

`NativeAppsHostMode` defaults to `edge`. The API's admission Layer registers one
60-per-60-second RateLimit binding and reads `CALCULATOR_RATE_NAMESPACE` through

attaches `taxkit.dev` (with a native `www.taxkit.dev` redirect) to the Website
and `api.taxkit.dev` to the API. Local and Preview graphs declare no domains.
The native redirect provider treats a failed shared-ruleset read as absence;
the focused provider test records that limit.

import * as HttpApiSchema from "./HttpApiSchema.ts"
import * as MediaType from "./internal/mediaType.ts"
import * as HttpApiPath from "./internal/path.ts"

/**
 * The type-safe client shape generated from HTTP API groups, with non-top-level
 * groups exposed as nested objects and top-level endpoints exposed as methods.
 *
 * @stability unstable
 * @category models
 * @since 4.0.0
 */
export type Client<Groups extends HttpApiGroup.Constraint, E = never, R = never> = Simplify<
  & {
    readonly [Group in Extract<Groups, { readonly topLevel: false }> as HttpApiGroup.Identifier<Group>]: Client.Group<
      Group,
      E,
      R
    >
  }
  & Client.TopLevelMethods<Groups, E, R>
>

/**
 * Derives the typed client interface for an `HttpApi`, preserving any additional
 * client error and service requirements supplied by the caller.
 *
 * @stability unstable
 * @category utility types
 * @since 4.0.0
 */
export type ForApi<Api extends HttpApi.Constraint, E = never, R = never> = Api extends
  HttpApi.HttpApi<infer _Id, infer Groups> ? Client<Groups, E, R> :
  never

/**
 * Computes the decoded success value a client receives for an endpoint
 * success schema, including headers, streaming Server-Sent Events, and
 * streaming byte responses.
 *
 * @stability unstable
 * @category utility types
 * @since 4.0.0
 */
export type SuccessType<S> = S extends HttpApiSchema.WithHeaders<
  infer _Inner,
  infer _Headers
> ? HttpApiSchema.withHeaders<SuccessType<_Inner>, _Headers["Type"]>
  : S extends HttpApiSchema.StreamSse<
    infer _Events,
    infer _Error,
 * @stability unstable
 * @category constructors
 * @since 4.0.0
 */
export const make = <ApiId extends string, Groups extends HttpApiGroup.Constraint>(
  api: HttpApi.HttpApi<ApiId, Groups>,
  options?: {
    readonly transformClient?: ((client: HttpClient.HttpClient) => HttpClient.HttpClient) | undefined
    readonly transformResponse?:
      | ((effect: Effect.Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown>) => Effect.Effect<unknown, unknown, unknown>)
      | undefined
    readonly baseUrl?: URL | string | undefined
  }
): Effect.Effect<
  Client<Groups>,
  never,
  HttpClient.HttpClient | HttpApiGroup.MiddlewareClient<Groups>
> =>
  Effect.flatMap(HttpClient.HttpClient, (httpClient) =>
    makeWith(api, {
      ...options,
      httpClient: options?.transformClient ? options.transformClient(httpClient) : httpClient
    }))

/**
 * Constructs a type-safe client for an HTTP API from the supplied `HttpClient`,
 * using the API metadata to encode requests, execute middleware, and decode
 * responses.
 *
 * @stability unstable
 * @category constructors
 * @since 4.0.0
 */
export const makeWith = <ApiId extends string, Groups extends HttpApiGroup.Constraint, E, R>(
  api: HttpApi.HttpApi<ApiId, Groups>,
  options: {
    readonly httpClient: HttpClient.HttpClient.With<E, R>
    readonly transformResponse?:

    readonly baseUrl?: URL | string | undefined

feat: deploy an unpatched one-way Website/API graph

The page doesn't answer this. It documents the Cache API (`caches.default`), and it states that Workers Caching is a separate mechanism: "The two mechanisms are independent." Its statements about Vary, Cache-Control, Set-Cookie, and cache keys therefore don't establish how Workers Cache behaves.

- **Vary:** The only Vary behavior described is in the Cache API. `cache.put` throws if the response contains "`Vary: *`". The `Vary` header is not in the list of headers the Cache API respects, and `ignoreVary` isn't supported on `match()`. Nothing here says whether Workers Cache honours `Vary: Origin` or `Vary: Accept`.
- **Cache-Control:** The Cache API respects it on `put()` and follows Cloudflare's Cache-Control directives. The page doesn't mention `CDN-Cache-Control`.
- **Set-Cookie:** Per the page, responses with `Set-Cookie` are never cached by the Cache API. The workaround is to remove the header or set `Cache-Control: private=Set-Cookie`.
- **Cache keys:** The Cache API uses the request as the key. The page notes that a custom cache key may strip the query string, and that `.workers.dev` includes the query string by default. It doesn't describe Workers Cache keys.
- **Tiered caching:** The page says `cache.put` isn't compatible with tiered caching and points to the fetch API for that. It doesn't describe the Workers Cache settings you mention.

For Workers Cache specifics, check the "How the cache works" reference the page links to.

Cloudflare's docs describe how `Vary` changes cache keys, though the results don't clearly explain how Workers-specific caching behaves when a Worker sits in front of an origin.

**How `Vary` affects the cache key:** The origin has to send the header. The origin response must include a `Vary` header. Once it does, the named request headers join the key, so one URL can have several cached versions. The listed request headers become part of the cache key for that response, following the HTTP caching behavior described in RFC 9111.

**Per-header actions:** Each listed header gets one of three behaviors. normalize collapses equivalent values, which suits most Accept, Accept-Language, and Accept-Encoding cases. passthrough uses the raw header value to select the cached version and forwards it to the origin unchanged. bypass bypasses cache whenever this header name appears in the origin's Vary response. A changelog entry dated 2026-07-02 introduced this feature for Cache Rules. A response containing `Vary: *` always bypasses cache, regardless of your Vary configuration.

**Where to configure it for Workers:** To configure Vary, use Vary in Cache Rules settings, or cf.vary for Workers subrequests. That means the cf.vary property applies to subrequests a Worker makes, not to the Worker's own incoming responses.

**Default Workers cache keys:** Headers outside the key are ignored. Requests that differ only in request headers that are not part of the cache key (for example, `User-Agent`, `Accept-Language`, `Cookie`, or `Authorization`) return the same cached response. The Workers cache docs suggest that if you do need content negotiation, set Vary on the response, or handle it inside your Worker and produce a canonical response per URL.

**Gaps:** The results don't say whether `caches.default` or the Cache API in a Worker honors an origin's `Vary` header the same way the CDN does. The Workers cache docs also reference a `cache.cross_version_cache` setting for per-version keying, which I couldn't examine in detail. For the exact behavior of a Worker sitting in front of a cache, check the Workers Cache configuration page directly, or test with a `curl` request that varies the header.

result.output:
**What the page says is in the cache key**

- **Target entrypoint:** The specific named entrypoint that received the request. "A `default` export and an exported class are different entrypoints" and don't share a cache.
- **Path and query string:** "Query parameter order matters," so `?a=1&b=2` and `?b=2&a=1` are separate keys. Trailing slashes also matter.
- **Worker version:** Included by default. "Each deployed version has its own cache," so a new deployment starts cold.
- **`ctx.props`:** Included when the Worker is invoked through a service binding or RPC.
- **Anti-cache-poisoning headers:** `x-http-method-override`, `x-http-method`, `x-method-override`, `x-forwarded-host`, `x-host`, `x-forwarded-scheme` (unless `http` or `https`), `x-original-url`, `x-rewrite-url`, and `forwarded` are included. The page also says `Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Key` is included when a caller sets it, and Cloudflare does not set it automatically.

**What the page says is not in the cache key**

- **HTTP method:** "`GET` and `HEAD` requests for the same URL share a single cache entry." The page says `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` are never cached.
- **Host:** "The cache key does not include the host," so one Worker shares a cache across all its domains.
- **Request body:** The page says it does not partition the cache.
- **Other request headers:** "Requests that differ only in request headers that are not part of the cache key… return the same cached response." Its examples are `User-Agent`, `Accept-Language`, `Cookie`, and `Authorization`.

**`Vary`**

The page says that for content negotiation you can "set `Vary` on the response, or handle it inside your Worker." It does not say which `Vary` values (such as Origin, Accept, or Cookie) are honored, so I can't confirm that from this page.

**`cache.cross_version_cache`**

The page says that setting `cache.cross_version_cache` to `true` drops the version from the cache key, so cached responses are shared across versions until they expire or are purged.

**`Set-Cookie`, `Authorization`, and bypass**

The page says Cloudflare's automatic bypass rules for `Set-Cookie` and `Authorization` can prevent caching problems "by disabling caching entirely for authenticated requests." It recommends `ctx.props` instead, since that still allows caching.

**Not covered on this page**

The page does not discuss how `Cache-Control`, `CDN-Cache-Control`, or `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` affect caching, and it does not describe default behavior for responses without `Cache-Control`. It only shows `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` and `public, max-age=3600` in examples. The "Configuration" and "Cache responses" pages it links to may cover these.

## Portable Oxlint rules

The canonical [Effect policy asset](../../assets/oxlint/effect-policy.ts) carries
the checks adapted from DAW's owned rules at `e47ecfb` and its qualified portable
extensions. Load this one owner
rather than combining unchanged plugins from several repositories. It uses
Effect and `@oxlint/plugins`; select exact compatible versions and qualify the
asset with the receiving repository's actual Oxlint command before enabling it.
Installed skill copies are distribution outputs, not editing surfaces.

Discover the currently installed plugin, then vendor the selected asset as a
byte-for-byte reference with its source revision and rule decisions recorded.
Do not edit installed plugin caches. An existing repository using installed
plugins needs only the selected lint asset; a deliberately qualified scaffold
snapshot follows its renderer's separate ownership and receipt contract.
Add the owned reference path to `jsPlugins`, qualify it with the
actual Oxlint command and choose these rules:

```ts
plugins: ["typescript"],
jsPlugins: ["./tools/oxlint/vendor/strict-effect/effect-policy.ts"],
rules: {
  "strict-effect/no-unchecked-index": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-native-at": "error",
  "strict-effect/runtime-file-convention": ["error", {
    webSourceRoots: ["apps/web/src"],
  }],
  "strict-effect/tagged-error-name": "error",
  "strict-effect/error-constructor-new": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-promise-workflow": ["error", { allowedFiles: [
    "apps/api/src/og/takumi.adapter.layer.ts",
  ] }],
  "strict-effect/no-unsafe-option-unwrap": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-unchecked-json": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-runtime-outside-boundary": ["error", {
    allowedFiles: ["apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts"],
  }],
  "strict-effect/no-native-work": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-imperative-collections": "error",
  "typescript/no-explicit-any": "error",
  "typescript/consistent-type-assertions": ["error", { assertionStyle: "never" }],
  "no-restricted-globals": ["error", {
    globals: ["fetch", "setTimeout", "setInterval", "Map", "Set"],
    checkGlobalObject: true,
  }],
  "no-restricted-properties": ["error",
    { object: "process", property: "env" },
    { object: "Bun", property: "env" },
    { object: "Date", property: "now" },
    { object: "Math", property: "random" },
  ],
},
```

Apply the checks to all owned TypeScript, including tests, tools, config and
infrastructure. Boundary paths are exact relative paths from Oxlint's working
directory; wildcards and parent paths do not grant an exception. Promise adapters
may declare a Promise return and use Promise.resolve; async/await, construction
and chains remain forbidden. The rule permits Effect's own catch operation.

`no-promise-workflow` also follows immutable local aliases, destructured helpers,
root namespaces and direct reads of `Effect.promise` and `Effect.tryPromise`.
It checks the nearest declaration, so a shadowed parameter does not borrow an
outer import's permission. When an existing host-contract test genuinely needs
only `Effect.promise`, configure its exact path in `promiseOnlyFiles`; this does
not allow `tryPromise`, raw Promise types, construction or chains. Do not allow
all tests or all files named `*.layer.ts`.

Use `strict-effect/module-ownership` for private SDKs, host bindings and authored
sources. Each `owners` entry supplies `module`, exact `allowedFiles` and explicit
`allowTypes`. Module names cover their subpaths. Set `allowTypes: true` for SDK
or host declarations when their types are public; set it to false when source
ownership also forbids type imports. Choose paths in the receiving repository,
not the shared skill. For example:

```ts
"strict-effect/module-ownership": ["error", { owners: [
  { module: "cloudflare:workers", allowedFiles: ["apps/web/src/lib/host.ingress.ts"], allowTypes: true },
  { module: "private-sdk", allowedFiles: ["packages/example/src/client.adapter.layer.ts"], allowTypes: true },
  { module: "@content/private", allowedFiles: ["apps/api/src/sources.ts"], allowTypes: false },
] }],
```

The rule checks static imports, re-exports, import-equals, import types and dynamic
imports. It resolves immutable local string aliases, templates and concatenation.
An unresolved dynamic address fails rather than escaping ownership checks.
Ordinary strings in build configuration are not imports. Prove the exact owner,
a neighbouring forbidden file, type-only permissions, unknown addresses and
all syntax forms with the actual Oxlint command. This checks source imports;
it does not prove a deployed bundle's contents.

`no-unsafe-option-unwrap` follows Effect imports, including aliases, to reject
Option.getOrThrow. `no-unchecked-json` rejects JSON.parse/stringify, their globalThis spellings and
raw web `.json()` calls. Use checked Schema codecs for both directions.
`no-runtime-outside-boundary` rejects ManagedRuntime.make and execution calls
outside approved files. Execution method names are reserved syntactically; do
not use runPromise or runSync as unrelated service method names. Import analysis
uses top-level bindings, not TypeScript's type checker; it does not prove that
aliased global JSON/Promise objects are safe. Keep code review and the other
strict checks alongside these rules. Actual negative and positive CLI fixtures
must prove the receiving config enables every promised rule.

The generated repository configuration also supplies actionable messages for
those standard restrictions. `no-native-work` rejects throws, try/catch, direct
environment reads, native current-time reads and ambient randomness. A Date
constructed from an explicit checked timestamp is a pure conversion and remains
allowed. The rule recognises direct and globalThis/window spellings; it does
not resolve arbitrary aliases, shadowing or dynamically computed names. Keep
review for those cases. It grants no whole-file host exception.

The receiving repository owns its workspace import rule and generated export
inventory. Enforce imports, re-exports and literal dynamic imports: packages
cannot depend on apps, and frontend code may import domain contracts and
transport clients rather than backend handlers, source loaders or live domain
implementations. Derive public export facts from manifests and keep a separate
explicit frontend policy. A successful typecheck alone cannot prove this
direction: a forbidden app export can still be valid TypeScript.

Merge these entries into the existing config; do not replace its other checks.
When replacing `unicorn/throw-new-error`, turn off only that overlapping rule
and record why. Keep prohibitions on throwing enabled.

| Check                     | Policy and limits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no-unchecked-index`      | Rejects all computed member reads, including literal keys. Use Effect Array/Record lookup and handle absence. Adopt this stricter policy deliberately; an unavoidable host access needs an exact exception.                                                                                                                                     |
| `no-native-at`            | Rejects reads/calls/aliases of `.at`; computed spellings are caught by the lookup rule. It matches the property name, not the receiver's inferred type.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `runtime-file-convention` | Rejects unqualified/reversed runtime filenames under configured source roots. Use `runtime.server.ts` and `runtime.client.ts`. A production browser build separately checks imports.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `tagged-error-name`       | Requires the class, self type and literal tag to agree. Recognises the current Schema.TaggedError factory through named/aliased/namespace/root imports.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `error-constructor-new`   | Requires `new` for `*Error` constructors, while allowing imported `Schema.TaggedError`, `Schema.Error` and `Data.TaggedError` class factories. Type-only imports and local functions do not grant the factory exception.                                                                                                                        |
| `no-promise-workflow`     | Rejects raw Promise workflows and imported `Effect.promise`/`Effect.tryPromise` outside exact `allowedFiles`. Recognises namespace, named, aliased and root imports, with lexical scope checks for conversion calls. An adapter allowance still requires native-first review; lint cannot determine whether every SDK has a native replacement. |

The import resolver follows top-level imports and static member paths. It is
not a complete scope/type analyser or arbitrary local-alias resolver. Keep
shadowing prohibited/reviewed; do not claim this syntactic check proves every
possible call. A rule that only matches a removed API can stay configured yet
do nothing. Verify installed exports and exercise the current spelling.
Do not add a Cloudflare binding allowance when the published Alchemy bridge
already owns conversion. Qualify aliases, shadowed names, neighbouring paths,
wildcard/parent-path rejection and accepted exact adapters with the real Oxlint
command, not source-pattern assertions alone.

For a project that explicitly chooses unpatched Alchemy, add the opt-in
[package-policy check](../../../alchemy-iac/assets/unpatched-alchemy.ts) to its
existing dependency checker. This is a manifest/lock/resolution check, not a
TypeScript lint rule. Supply real parsed documents and installed manifests for
every declared importing owner. Exercise active root/workspace/lock patches,
mixed versions, missing resolution evidence, unrelated package patches and
malformed lock data. Fresh-install, bundle and saved-state proof remain separate;
follow [native migrations](../../../alchemy-iac/references/operations/native-migrations.md).

Extend the existing fixture suite with invalid _and valid_ cases for imports,
aliases, factory calls and configured runtime paths. Require the actual
Oxlint command to examine the intended file, return a failing exit with the
expected rule for a negative case, and return cleanly for the valid case.
Regex-only tests do not prove that the plugin is loaded. Keep imported snapshots
unchanged with their revision/hash and disposition; edit owned portable rules
at their canonical owner. Document exact adapter exceptions and false positives,
such as `Output.map` being mistaken for an array method.

## Native request ownership

Use these checks when the Website reads a separate public API. They live in the
same portable policy asset, not another plugin or custom request runtime.

| Rule                       | What it rejects                                                                                                                                                            | What stays valid                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no-loader-request-state`  | Native request Atom/result-cache construction inside recognised TanStack loaders or exact loader owners; loader reads of locally inspectable configured-client query Atoms | Component query Atoms, local appearance/progress state, direct native client calls, configuration/service Atom reads |
| `no-native-client-replica` | A `Layer.effect` service whose entire locally inspectable implementation copies or simply forwards generated `HttpApiClient` methods                                       | Complete-request deadlines, input selection, validation, domain mapping and named feature errors                     |
| `checked-page-response`    | Repeated format comparisons after a configured checked helper selected a literal format; repeated decoding of its response with the configured complete response Schema    | Runtime-union narrowing, page/path/title/course checks and different domain/view Schemas                             |
| `native-cloudflare-cache`  | Reads of the global Cache API, including scoped immutable aliases and destructuring                                                                                        | Native Alchemy Worker/Website cache declarations, native cache operations and Effect caches for backend work         |
| `website-data-proxy`       | Native TanStack server handlers at configured public API paths or their descendants in the Website source directory                                                        | HTML loaders, finished downloads, discovery, MCP and analytics routes outside those paths                            |

Configure actual owner paths and import addresses. Do not copy example names
into a different repository. Enable the cache rule only where native Alchemy
owns the Cloudflare cache. The checked-response rule is opt-in: first establish
that the named helper already validates the requested format and full reply.
It must not discourage checking an unchecked external response once.

```ts
"strict-effect/no-loader-request-state": ["error", {
  loaderFiles: ["apps/web/src/lib/page.loader.ts"],
  clientServices: [{ module: "../lib/runtime.client", name: "ApiClient" }],
}],
"strict-effect/no-native-client-replica": "error",
"strict-effect/checked-page-response": ["error", {
  checkedHelper: { module: "apps/web/src/lib/api/requests", export: "requestPage" },
  responseSchema: { module: "@example/content/schemas", export: "PageResponse" },
}],
"strict-effect/native-cloudflare-cache": "error",
"strict-effect/website-data-proxy": ["error", {
  websiteDirectory: "apps/web/src",
  publicApiPaths: ["/pages", "/courses"],
}],
```

Qualify each enabled rule through the real Oxlint command with forbidden and
valid examples. Include renamed imports, immutable aliases, local shadowing,
configuration Atom reads and feature policy. The checks inspect local syntax and
import identity. They do not follow arbitrary inter-module values, object
spreads, function-returned clients, all indirect route options or every possible
Layer construction. A service with additional real policy is intentionally not
rejected merely because another method forwards a request. Review remains
responsible for whether that policy belongs there. These rules never prove
hosted cache hits, CORS, deadlines or cancellation; use separate runtime tests
and public response evidence.

Inspect the actual cloned Effect and Alchemy sources, installed APIs and current Common Practice. Remove unnecessary wrappers, approval/receipt ceremony, and ALL Alchemy patches while preserving tax correctness, public machine clients and privacy. Prioritise Cloudflare, with Bun as a supported secondary host. Run meaningful checks and native Alchemy/Doppler deployments locally from this Mac/worktree, not GitHub Actions. Cooper explicitly authorises the necessary commits, PRs/pushes, merging this goal's checked changes into TaxKit main, and publishing and checking the Production Website/API pair. This supersedes the earlier review-only scope and duplicate receipt/approval requirements for these same operations. Do not ask again for the already-approved merge or deployments. Create/activate this as a persistent goal if the goal facility is available and work through completion. Do not stop at a plan. Read the full saved goal before coding; it includes the practical local checks, known upstream limits, rollback and delivery criteria. Report concrete blockers clearly. Your first response should confirm the actual worktree path and that the full handover has been read.

   **Security and authority constraints from GOAL.md (still in force):**
   - It does not authorise unrelated infrastructure changes, npm/package publication, new credentials, wider credential permissions, billing changes, deleting unrelated resources or patches in other projects.
   - Do not implement in `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit` or disturb its dirty changes. Do not reset or overwrite other worktrees or branches.

   **Agreed design (GOAL.md):**
   1. Cloudflare first; Bun kept as a secondary host with one shared capacity pool.
   2. Native HTTP for Website data:
      - Server rendering uses `HttpApiClient` over the private binding (Alchemy `fromCloudflareFetcher`/`toHttpClient`), plus the trusted `calculatorRequest` for calculation.

      - No `createServerFn`, Website proxy, envelopes or replica services.
      - Add API discovery GET/HEAD handlers; the Website forwards them once.
   3. One registry is created before loaders and shared with React. TanStack owns loader data; no request atoms.
   4. Q5: replace `createTaxKitApiClient`, `withTaxKitHttpApiClient` and `createTaxKitApiClientLayer` and their aliases with native clients. Make `TakeHomeScenarioLiveFromInput` and `AnnualTaxScenarioLiveFromInput` static Layers, with Changesets.
   5. Q6: public credential-free browser access for valid HTTP(S) origins. Publication origin is `https://taxkit.dev`. API endpoint addresses stay stage-specific. No reverse Website Output into the API.
   6. Q7: native version-scoped cache on both Workers:
      - Public successes: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0` and `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-if-error=0`.
      - Private, error and Set-Cookie replies are not cached.
      - Content changes must rebuild both Workers.
      - Prove HIT/Age, variants in both orders, and a Preview content-only change; restore the fixture before Production.
   7. Q8: MCP `allowedOrigins` is `["https://taxkit.dev"]`. Keep the legacy early origin/quota guard.

   10. Safe operational fields only.

   **Checks that must hold:**
   - 5 s / 64 KiB POST body read, 5 s calculation work, 10 s full reply, 2 MiB cap.
   - Trusted `calculatorRequest` admits POST `/rpc` and the canonical HTTP calculate route.
   - The bounded adapter keeps real statuses, headers and 4xx/5xx bodies, and times the whole call.
   - Vendor the 0.7.1 `effect-policy.ts` byte for byte with a provenance note; enable the native loader/client/cache/proxy rules with real Oxlint fixtures.
   - Remove ceremony checks.

        block=lines[i:j+1]

        m=re.search(r"files: \[(.*?)\]", text, re.S)
        files=re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', m.group(1)) if m else None
        keep=True

            globs=[f for f in files if "*" in f]

            rules=re.findall(r'^        "([^"]+)":', text, re.M)

        # preceding comment lines belong to block (they are inside braces) fine

`Cache-Control: public, max-age=0` and seven-day Cloudflare freshness; every
other reply, including calculations, errors and cookie-setting responses, is
`no-store` for both browsers and Cloudflare.

replaces `websiteOrigin` with `publicationOrigin`, checked by the new
`DocsPublicationOrigin` Schema, so canonical links name the published site even
when a separate Preview serves the page. The acceptance-record Schemas
(`PublicPageAcceptanceRecord`, its versions and `DocsAcceptedSourceDigest`) are
removed; page frontmatter now decides publication. Packages use Effect 4.0.2.

Both server Layers require the caller's `ContentService`. API hosts supply the
accepted build output; the HTTP package imports only the compiled content
contracts. The native API host supplies its shared calculator service to HTTP
and RPC.

The `content` group delegates navigation, page lookup and search to that same
content service. Markdown returns the owning processed page body as
`text/markdown`. Page queries use checked, bounded public addresses; search
terms have the owning 100-character limit. Missing pages return fixed typed
JSON 404 guidance and a search-source failure returns fixed typed JSON 503
guidance, without reflecting paths or source-error messages. Native invalid
query responses are empty 400 replies. This surface returns accepted public
documentation only, not personal calculation reports.

`TaxKitApiInProcessClientLive` also requires supplied content. It now uses the
native Effect HTTP client and router in the caller's Layer scope; each request
closes its own scope. It creates no web-handler runner or Promise bridge.
Its generated client checks the same response Schemas as remote consumers.

## Runtime Shape

The package is built as ESM TypeScript. Runtime exports are split by boundary:

- browser-safe consumers should use `@taxkit/api-http/client`

- app or test code that needs in-process wiring can use the client layers
- handler exports are server-side and should not be imported from browser code

`ApiRoutesLive` owns reusable route middleware such as CORS inside this package.
App packages should provide a platform HTTP server and process config, not
duplicate API route middleware.

## Establish the boundary

Define owned TypeScript paths and exact exceptions:

- application/package source: strict;
- tests: strict, with deterministic test APIs;
- host adapters: narrow allowed bridge;
- generated/vendor: excluded by exact path;
- configuration files: classify individually;
- migrations: strict for I/O and errors even if historical data shapes are plain.

Do not disable a rule repository-wide for one host constraint.
After moving code, run the actual Oxlint command on negative fixtures under the
new packages, apps, tools and test paths. Include a valid fixture so the check
also proves the intended native Effect code is accepted. A rule configured only
for the former app path can silently leave the new package unprotected.

## Static restrictions

Use lint/architecture tests to forbid or restrict:

- `async` functions and `new Promise`;
- raw `fetch`;
- direct environment access;
- `console.*`;
- ambient time/random/timers;
- unchecked JSON;
- `any` and unsafe assertions;
- `Effect.run*` outside runtime files;
- provider SDK imports outside approved live adapters;
- generic raw client exports;
- mutable globals;
- native Map/Set in domain paths;
- package imports of application runtimes.

Rules should report the approved alternative and exact adapter path policy.

## Portable Oxlint rules

The canonical [Effect policy asset](../../assets/oxlint/effect-policy.ts) carries
the checks adapted from DAW's owned rules at `e47ecfb` and its qualified portable
extensions. Load this one owner
rather than combining unchanged plugins from several repositories. It uses
Effect and `@oxlint/plugins`; select exact compatible versions and qualify the
asset with the receiving repository's actual Oxlint command before enabling it.
Installed skill copies are distribution outputs, not editing surfaces.

Discover the currently installed plugin, then vendor the selected asset as a
byte-for-byte reference with its source revision and rule decisions recorded.
Do not edit installed plugin caches. An existing repository using installed
plugins needs only the selected lint asset; a deliberately qualified scaffold
snapshot follows its renderer's separate ownership and receipt contract.
Add the owned reference path to `jsPlugins`, qualify it with the
actual Oxlint command and choose these rules:

```ts
plugins: ["typescript"],
jsPlugins: ["./tools/oxlint/vendor/strict-effect/effect-policy.ts"],
rules: {
  "strict-effect/no-unchecked-index": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-native-at": "error",
  "strict-effect/runtime-file-convention": ["error", {
    webSourceRoots: ["apps/web/src"],
  }],
  "strict-effect/tagged-error-name": "error",
  "strict-effect/error-constructor-new": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-promise-workflow": ["error", { allowedFiles: [
    "apps/api/src/og/takumi.adapter.layer.ts",
  ] }],
  "strict-effect/no-unsafe-option-unwrap": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-unchecked-json": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-runtime-outside-boundary": ["error", {
    allowedFiles: ["apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts"],
  }],
  "strict-effect/no-native-work": "error",
  "strict-effect/no-imperative-collections": "error",
  "typescript/no-explicit-any": "error",
  "typescript/consistent-type-assertions": ["error", { assertionStyle: "never" }],
  "no-restricted-globals": ["error", {
    globals: ["fetch", "setTimeout", "setInterval", "Map", "Set"],
    checkGlobalObject: true,
  }],
  "no-restricted-properties": ["error",
    { object: "process", property: "env" },
    { object: "Bun", property: "env" },
    { object: "Date", property: "now" },
    { object: "Math", property: "random" },
  ],
},
```

Apply the checks to all owned TypeScript, including tests, tools, config and
infrastructure. Boundary paths are exact relative paths from Oxlint's working
directory; wildcards and parent paths do not grant an exception. Promise adapters
may declare a Promise return and use Promise.resolve; async/await, construction
and chains remain forbidden. The rule permits Effect's own catch operation.

`no-promise-workflow` also follows immutable local aliases, destructured helpers,
root namespaces and direct reads of `Effect.promise` and `Effect.tryPromise`.
It checks the nearest declaration, so a shadowed parameter does not borrow an
outer import's permission. When an existing host-contract test genuinely needs
only `Effect.promise`, configure its exact path in `promiseOnlyFiles`; this does
not allow `tryPromise`, raw Promise types, construction or chains. Do not allow
all tests or all files named `*.layer.ts`.

Use `strict-effect/module-ownership` for private SDKs, host bindings and authored
sources. Each `owners` entry supplies `module`, exact `allowedFiles` and explicit
`allowTypes`. Module names cover their subpaths. Set `allowTypes: true` for SDK
or host declarations when their types are public; set it to false when source
ownership also forbids type imports. Choose paths in the receiving repository,
not the shared skill. For example:

```ts
"strict-effect/module-ownership": ["error", { owners: [
  { module: "cloudflare:workers", allowedFiles: ["apps/web/src/lib/host.ingress.ts"], allowTypes: true },
  { module: "private-sdk", allowedFiles: ["packages/example/src/client.adapter.layer.ts"], allowTypes: true },
  { module: "@content/private", allowedFiles: ["apps/api/src/sources.ts"], allowTypes: false },
] }],
```

The rule checks static imports, re-exports, import-equals, import types and dynamic
imports. It resolves immutable local string aliases, templates and concatenation.
An unresolved dynamic address fails rather than escaping ownership checks.
Ordinary strings in build configuration are not imports. Prove the exact owner,
a neighbouring forbidden file, type-only permissions, unknown addresses and
all syntax forms with the actual Oxlint command. This checks source imports;
it does not prove a deployed bundle's contents.

`no-unsafe-option-unwrap` follows Effect imports, including aliases, to reject
Option.getOrThrow. `no-unchecked-json` rejects JSON.parse/stringify, their globalThis spellings and
raw web `.json()` calls. Use checked Schema codecs for both directions.
`no-runtime-outside-boundary` rejects ManagedRuntime.make and execution calls
outside approved files. Execution method names are reserved syntactically; do
not use runPromise or runSync as unrelated service method names. Import analysis
uses top-level bindings, not TypeScript's type checker; it does not prove that
aliased global JSON/Promise objects are safe. Keep code review and the other
strict checks alongside these rules. Actual negative and positive CLI fixtures
must prove the receiving config enables every promised rule.

## Native request ownership

Use these checks when the Website reads a separate public API. They live in the
same portable policy asset, not another plugin or custom request runtime.

| Rule                       | What it rejects                                                                                                                                                            | What stays valid                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no-loader-request-state`  | Native request Atom/result-cache construction inside recognised TanStack loaders or exact loader owners; loader reads of locally inspectable configured-client query Atoms | Component query Atoms, local appearance/progress state, direct native client calls, configuration/service Atom reads |
| `no-native-client-replica` | A `Layer.effect` service whose entire locally inspectable implementation copies or simply forwards generated `HttpApiClient` methods                                       | Complete-request deadlines, input selection, validation, domain mapping and named feature errors                     |
| `checked-page-response`    | Repeated format comparisons after a configured checked helper selected a literal format; repeated decoding of its response with the configured complete response Schema    | Runtime-union narrowing, page/path/title/course checks and different domain/view Schemas                             |
| `native-cloudflare-cache`  | Reads of the global Cache API, including scoped immutable aliases and destructuring                                                                                        | Native Alchemy Worker/Website cache declarations, native cache operations and Effect caches for backend work         |
| `website-data-proxy`       | Native TanStack server handlers at configured public API paths or their descendants in the Website source directory                                                        | HTML loaders, finished downloads, discovery, MCP and analytics routes outside those paths                            |

Configure actual owner paths and import addresses. Do not copy example names
into a different repository. Enable the cache rule only where native Alchemy
owns the Cloudflare cache. The checked-response rule is opt-in: first establish
that the named helper already validates the requested format and full reply.
It must not discourage checking an unchecked external response once.

```ts
"strict-effect/no-loader-request-state": ["error", {
  loaderFiles: ["apps/web/src/lib/page.loader.ts"],
  clientServices: [{ module: "../lib/runtime.client", name: "ApiClient" }],
}],
"strict-effect/no-native-client-replica": "error",
"strict-effect/checked-page-response": ["error", {
  checkedHelper: { module: "apps/web/src/lib/api/requests", export: "requestPage" },
  responseSchema: { module: "@example/content/schemas", export: "PageResponse" },
}],
"strict-effect/native-cloudflare-cache": "error",
"strict-effect/website-data-proxy": ["error", {
  websiteDirectory: "apps/web/src",
  publicApiPaths: ["/pages", "/courses"],
}],
```

Qualify each enabled rule through the real Oxlint command with forbidden and
valid examples. Include renamed imports, immutable aliases, local shadowing,
configuration Atom reads and feature policy. The checks inspect local syntax and
import identity. They do not follow arbitrary inter-module values, object
spreads, function-returned clients, all indirect route options or every possible
Layer construction. A service with additional real policy is intentionally not
rejected merely because another method forwards a request. Review remains
responsible for whether that policy belongs there. These rules never prove
hosted cache hits, CORS, deadlines or cancellation; use separate runtime tests
and public response evidence.

Progress so far (nothing committed since the last checkpoint):

- **Lint:** the 0.7.1 strict policy is vendored and now enforced. Promise exceptions are limited to an exact list of host adapters and tests. Overrides for deleted files are gone.
- **Native rules:** the loader, client-copy, cache, Website-proxy, runtime, module-ownership and static-Layer rules are on. 15 real Oxlint fixture tests check them.
- **Q5:**
  - The api-http client helpers are gone; callers use `HttpApiClient` directly.
  - `./in-process` replaces `./client/server`.
  - Scenario Layers are static.
  - Changesets are added.
  - Tests pass: api-http 46, calculators 41, SDK 58, docs-examples 9, API 114, web unit 85 and web browser 23.
- **Bun host:**
  - It now uses the same public CORS policy as the Worker: any exact HTTP(S) origin, no credentials.
  - Its eight-place calculation pool was already shared across all requests, as reading the source confirms. I haven't added a test for that.
- **Saved skill copies:** the copied shared skills and their links are removed. The repo's own guidance says these come from the published plugin, not saved copies.

Two background agents are still running: one is updating the native Website/API pair tests, the other is converting the remaining Layer factories in packages to static Layers. When they finish I'll make the RPC test-client Layers static, update the docs, commit, then open the PR, merge and deploy.

The server's binding client still sends these headers; I left it alone because no test covers it, but the old setup didn't send them either.

- **Pages that fail to load return 500, not 503.** `rejectServerLoad` sets 503, but the framework's error handling overrides it. This affects the settings failure, a docs page whose content doesn't match its compiled build, and an unavailable search. Unavailable search used to return 200, so 500 is safer: it can no longer be cached publicly. The tests assert 500 plus `no-store`.
- **An unreadable or invalid API calculation reply now shows "The TaxKit service could not be reached"** (`WebsiteApiUnavailable`). It used to show "Check your details". `WebsiteApiMismatch` might fit a malformed reply better; that's your call.

One isolated run failed earlier on a timing race that predates these changes (clicking Calculate before the page finished hydrating). It passed on rerun and in the full run.
- **`native-analytics`** (this is the "forwards fresh browser and HTML collection choices" test you listed under relay): it was timing out waiting for a `/rpc` response; it now waits for the calculate POST.
- **`native-browser-tools`:** separates API reads from calculations. The catalogue tool must issue exactly `GET /api/v1/calculators`, the calculations must match exactly, and any `/rpc` or `/_serverFn` call fails the test. Held-request checks now use the annual calculate route.

Cooper asked me (the Site DEV-119 session) to have you check TaxKit against a Workers Cache bug found in Site and Common Practice, and fix it if it applies.

The bug: when a page's HTML and another response at the same URL (an Accept-negotiated Markdown response or redirect, or a 400/406 negotiation reply) carry different `Vary` headers, Workers Cache keeps evicting one with the other. On Site preview and Common Practice production, the HTML had `Vary: Accept, Cookie` and the Markdown 307 had `Vary: Accept`. The HTML was then a MISS after every Markdown request, whichever came first. Content stays correct; only cache reuse is lost.

Your worktree (taxkit-native-effect-alchemy-f44f82) enables `cache({ crossVersionCache: false })` on the API Worker. `apps/web/src/lib/docs/markdown.response.server.ts` sets and merges `vary: Accept` for docs Markdown. Please check whether the docs HTML at the same URLs carries exactly the same Vary set, and whether any HTML varies on Cookie.

The rule is now published in development-workflows 0.7.2 (commonplace-plugins main@32cff8e, PR #51):
1. Every response served at one URL must carry the same `Vary` set. Discovery files at their own URLs keep their own set. See `alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md`, "Native public response caching".
2. Public HTML must not vary on `Cookie`. A saved theme is applied before first paint with TanStack's `ScriptOnce`, with `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`. See `strict-effect-ts/references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md`, "Theme and appearance before first paint".

Hosted proof Cooper wants, where the website is cached:
- At one fresh docs URL: HTML, the Markdown variant, HTML, then the reverse order. Every repeat must be a HIT.
- HTML with and without an unrelated cookie is shared.

If TaxKit isn't affected, record that with the evidence. Please handle it after your current work, through your normal checks and delivery. I won't edit your repo.

content.text:
I've checked TaxKit against the cached-HTML eviction bug (mismatched `Vary` headers at one URL). By reading the code, TaxKit isn't affected, but that isn't confirmed by a test run or on a deployed site yet.

- **No cookie in HTML:** nothing reads a cookie when building pages, so HTML never varies on `Cookie`.
- **Docs pages:** the HTML, the Markdown version and the 400/406/404/503 negotiation replies at a docs URL all carry `Vary: Accept`.
- **API:** the shared CORS policy adds `Vary: Origin` to every reply, with or without an `Origin` header, so one URL always has the same set.

The open point is whether TanStack adds any other `Vary` value to page HTML. I've tightened the native pair test to require exactly `Vary: Accept` on docs HTML, and will run it once verification finishes.

On Preview I'll run the HIT checks you asked for: HTML, Markdown, HTML at a fresh docs URL, then the reverse order, plus HTML with and without an unrelated cookie.
